title: Tenant namespace collision causing KV-prefix cache poisoning — root cause analysis and mitigation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 a capacity event exposed a correctness regression in the KV/prefix cache that allowed cross-tenant cache entries to be served (observed as 'poisoned' prefixes). This manifested as incorrect completions for a small number of requests and, in two cases, short-lived exposure of prompt metadata from one tenant to another. The immediate incident led to elevated error rates and a brief rollback to the previous cache layout.

Scope: ~0.02% of total requests during the incident window, but high-severity because of cross-tenant data boundaries. Root cause is a change in the compacted prefix hashing map plus a race condition in the compaction path that omitted tenant-scoped namespace prefixes under specific shard-rebalance sequences. The compaction/hardening change shipped in runtime-1.20 to improve slab utilization accidentally relied on a derived key that could be collapsed across tenants when a suffix strip optimization was applied under memory pressure.

Impact: brief data exposure for <30 requests (investigation ongoing), elevated 5xx rates for serving nodes participating in compaction, and repeated eviction oscillation that impaired throughput for several minutes. No evidence of persisted long-term cross-tenant contamination post-mitigation.

root_cause: A suffix-strip micro-optimization in the compaction path (aimed at reducing key length for cache keys) combined with a race during shard-rebalance/compaction that allowed the derived key to be computed without the tenant prefix in a narrow timing window. This produced identical cache keys across different tenants which then allowed a served cache entry to be selected for the wrong tenant. The change lacked an explicit invariant test for tenant namespace preservation and the CI workload did not cover concurrent rebalance + compaction under memory pressure.
immediate_mitigations: Disabled suffix-strip optimization on all clusters (hot rollback) - 2026-03-09
Forced a restart of affected serving nodes to flush potentially poisoned slabs
Applied emergency server-side check: reject cache reads where 'tenant_id' header mismatches cache's stored namespace metadata
Raised alerting thresholds to detect any future namespace mismatch within 1 minute

acceptance_criteria:
1) CI job reproduces previous race within a reproducible harness and fails until the fix is applied.
2) Hotfix merged and canary run for 48 hours with zero namespace-mismatch alerts.
3) New telemetry surfaces namespace mismatch events as alerts in the daily dashboards.
4) Security review completed and compliance report filed.
5) Rollout checklist accepted in runtime team's RFC and added to per-release gates.
notes_and_tradeoffs: We chose enforcement at key generation (explicit tenant prefix) as the first long-term fix because it provides a minimal performance cost with maximal isolation guarantees. Alternative designs (stronger slab tagging or per-tenant slabs) are higher cost operationally and will be evaluated in Q2. There is a short-term throughput hit in canary because of increased key length, but telemetry shows <0.7% P50 token latency regression under typical load. We will explore a safe-encoding to regain that overhead if needed.
